summary.summary: A two-page covering summary of Newark and Sherwood's year-end treasury position ahead of Full Council on 14 July 2026, prepared on draft accounts. Total borrowings fell from £109.799m to £104.923m over 2025/26, putting total external debt (including £6.297m of other long-term liabilities) at £111.220m. Investments fell from £49.028m to £38.140m, of which £12.5m is long-term. The council states there were no breaches of approved prudential indicators; all the detail (CFR, maturity profile, indicator tables) sits in Appendix A, a separate agenda document.

news_drafts.headline: Newark and Sherwood faces £2.1m income shortfall on subsidiary loans three months into year
news_drafts.lead: Newark and Sherwood District Council has received only £118,000 of the £2.573m it budgeted for this year from loans to subsidiaries in the first quarter, a shortfall that reverses the General Fund's expected finances from net income to net costs. If the rate continues, annual income will reach roughly £472,000 — leaving a £2.1m gap the council must fill from reserves or spending cuts. The council is otherwise meeting prudential borrowing limits and remains compliant with the indicators that measure debt sustainability. Its auditors have flagged a control weakness — the Financial Services Manager can create and approve their own journal entries without independent review — and have identified disclosure gaps in complex accounting areas, though none has pushed the accounts out of line with accepted standards.

findings.paper_title: Newark and Sherwood District Council-Progress Report (SICA) September 2026-f(r)
findings.headline: Planning enforcement cases are acted upon within target timeframes at 95% or above, though audit testing found cases with extended periods of inactivity
findings.detail: Planning enforcement cases are actioned within the Planning Enforcement Plan's target timeframes 95% or above. However, testing of 20 cases found 3 with no recorded activity for 6-12 months, 1 returned Planning Contravention Notice not acted on for months, and 2 cases marked as resolved but still open. Management attributed these gaps to workload prioritization and annual leave, and is implementing bimonthly workload reviews and a monitoring dashboard.
findings.matters: Strong performance against published targets (95%+) indicates core service effectiveness. However, underlying case management issues suggest capacity or process controls need tightening to prevent cases stalling despite hitting overall timelines.
findings.figures: 95% or above on target timeframes; 20 cases tested; 3 with 6-12 months no recorded activity; 1 returned PCN not acted on; 2 cases marked resolved but still open
findings.quote: The actioning of enforcement cases within the target timeframes set out in the Planning Enforcement Plan for FY2025/26 are consistently 95% or above.

findings.paper_title: Newark and Sherwood District Council-Progress Report (SICA) September 2026-f(r)
findings.headline: Damp and Mould policy and procedures remain overdue 11 months after Awaab's Law statutory deadline
findings.detail: The council was required to update its Damp and Mould Policy and Responding to Damp & Mould Procedure by October 2025 to comply with Awaab's Law, which took effect 27th October 2025. As of September 2026, both updates remain overdue. A related Priority 1 recommendation on implementing centralized damp and mould case tracking has been rescheduled from November 2025 to 30th September 2026, though interim tracking solutions are in place.
findings.matters: Awaab's Law is a statutory requirement with explicit timescales. Non-compliance creates legal and regulatory risk and may indicate broader compliance capability concerns.
findings.figures: Original due dates 10/10/2025 and 24/10/2025; report dated 3rd September 2026; Priority 1 recommendation rescheduled from 26/11/2025 to 30/09/2026
findings.quote: This is currently being updated to reflect introduction of Awaabs Law from 27th October.

findings.paper_title: Newark and Sherwood District Council-Progress Report (SICA) September 2026-f(r)
findings.headline: Business continuity planning lacks clear communications accountability and adequate testing; council has declined to implement prior-year Priority 1 recommendation
findings.detail: The audit found multiple control weaknesses: communications responsibility is unclear across corporate and service business continuity plans; 3 of 10 critical service plans have never been tested; 7 tested plans lack documented action logs or lessons learned; 6 lack clearly identified systems to assess alignment with ICT recovery objectives. The council has declined the prior-year Priority 1 recommendation to implement full phased testing, instead planning ad-hoc annual scenarios. No formal BC training programme exists for staff or new starters.
findings.matters: Business continuity is foundational to operational resilience. Control gaps and inadequate testing leave the council's ability to maintain services during disruptions unproven. Declining a Priority 1 recommendation indicates governance weakness in managing audit findings.
findings.figures: 3 of 10 critical service business continuity plans never tested; 7 tested without action logs; 6 without clearly identified systems; Emergency Response risk register rating red/12 (target amber/6)
findings.quote: Discussions indicate that the Council does not intend to implement the recommendation to implement a full phased testing programme and will instead decide which business continuity scenario to test on an annual basis.

findings.paper_title: 23.09.26 - Budget Monitoring as at 30 Jun 26 - Appendix A
findings.headline: 64.4% of borrowing matures beyond 10 years, locking long-term debt service obligations
findings.detail: The borrowing maturity structure concentrates 64.38% of debt in the 10+ year bucket, 6.24% in 5–10 years, 8.39% in 2–5 years, 14.83% in 1–2 years, and 6.15% within 12 months. This long-dated structure provides certainty on debt service but extends obligations into the 2030s and beyond.
findings.matters: Debt maturity profile directly affects refinancing risk and long-term affordability. High proportions of long-dated debt reduce short-term refinancing pressure but commit the council to fixed costs across extended periods, limiting financial flexibility.
findings.figures: Maturity 10+ years 64.38%, 5–10 years 6.24%, 2–5 years 8.39%, 1–2 years 14.83%, under 12 months 6.15%

findings.paper_title: 23.09.26 - Budget Monitoring as at 30 Jun 26 - Appendix A
findings.headline: Council has deployed £15.2m in service investment loans to subsidiaries, with £11.3m capacity remaining
findings.detail: Of the £26.5m lending limit approved for service investments, £15.2m has been deployed, of which £15.186m is to subsidiaries. £4.001m has been invested in subsidiary shareholdings out of £5m approved. This represents significant financial exposure to subsidiary performance.
findings.matters: Service investment loans and equity in subsidiaries create contingent liabilities. Poor subsidiary performance generates calls for capital injection or loan write-offs. A lender assessing the council's true financial exposure needs to understand these risks and the income dependency on them.
findings.figures: Service investment loans deployed £15.202m of £26.5m limit; subsidiary loans £15.186m of £25m limit; subsidiary shareholdings £4.001m of £5m limit
